message.content: Do a PR review on PR 119

findings.short_summary: Old-path ignore rules dropped; leftovers become untracked
findings.summary: The ignore rules for the old paths (`SwitchboardMobile/Config/Local.xcconfig`, `SwitchboardMobile/SwitchboardMobileKit/{Generated,.build,.swiftpm}/`, `crates/app/gen/`) were replaced rather than kept alongside the new ones, so files those rules hid in existing checkouts now show up as untracked.
findings.failure_scenario: A developer who ran `make ios-crypto` or set up device signing before the move runs `git pull`. Git leaves the ignored files at the old paths. `git status` then lists `SwitchboardMobile/Config/Local.xcconfig` (their personal Apple team id), the generated xcframework binaries and `crates/app/gen/schemas/*.json` as untracked. A later `git add -A` commits all of them. Verified: `git check-ignore` reports all four paths as not ignored. Cargo.toml line 8 and ios/README.md both acknowledge these leftovers, but .gitignore no longer covers them.

findings.short_summary: make check fails on leftover SwiftPM build JSON
findings.summary: Prettier 3 skips whatever .gitignore ignores, so once the old `SwitchboardMobile/...` rules are gone, `pnpm format:check` (run by `make lint`, `make check` and `make check-frontend`) starts scanning leftover SwiftPM build JSON. `.prettierignore` only adds `ios/`, not the old path.
findings.failure_scenario: An existing checkout that has built the iOS package has `SwitchboardMobile/SwitchboardMobileKit/.build/*.json`. After pulling, `make check` fails with `[warn] SwitchboardMobile/SwitchboardMobileKit/.build/workspace-state.json ... Code style issues found`. Reproduced on the PR branch: format:check exits 1.

findings.summary: `dev`, `build` and `debug-app` gained an `install` prerequisite, but `test`, `lint` and `test-browser` (which now run through `pnpm --dir desktop`) did not.
findings.failure_scenario: In a pre-move checkout, `git pull && make test` or `make lint` runs `pnpm --dir desktop test` / `eslint` with no `desktop/node_modules`. It either fails to find vitest or eslint, or, if a stale root `node_modules` happens to supply them, quietly runs against stale root-hoisted copies. Running `make dev` first would have installed the workspace. (Not reproduced; I didn't run this in a pre-move checkout.)

findings.short_summary: make dev reinstalls every start; two instances race
findings.summary: Making `install` a prerequisite of `dev` means every `make dev` runs the Node version check plus `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`. Two side-by-side instances (`make dev DEV_PORT=1421`, the workflow AGENTS.md describes) now race two installs on one `node_modules`.
findings.failure_scenario: The developer starts `make dev` and `make dev DEV_PORT=1421` together in one checkout after a lockfile change. The two concurrent pnpm installs collide and one instance fails to start (AGENTS.md now documents this and says to rerun). Every dev start also pays the install. A cheaper option is to run the install only when `pnpm-lock.yaml` is newer than a stamp file such as `node_modules/.modules.yaml`.

findings.short_summary: AGENTS.md still points to root `pnpm test`
findings.summary: The Browser test bullet still says 'the default `make test` / `pnpm test` stays jsdom-only', but the root package.json no longer has a `test` script. That script now lives only in `desktop/package.json`.
findings.failure_scenario: Following AGENTS.md (which now says 'Run every command from the repo root'), an agent or developer runs `pnpm test` at the root and gets a missing-script error instead of the jsdom suite. The working command is `pnpm --dir desktop test` or `make test`.

findings.short_summary: Perf harness run instructions use pre-move paths
findings.summary: The manual run instructions (`VITE_PERF=1 pnpm vitest run --project browser tests/browser/perf-baseline.browser.test.ts`) still assume vitest, the vite config and `tests/` sit at the repo root.
findings.failure_scenario: Run from the repo root, as the reorganized docs instruct: vitest is not installed at the root (the root package has only prettier) and `tests/browser/...` no longer exists there. The perf harness can't be run as written. It needs `pnpm --dir desktop vitest ...`.

findings.short_summary: Ignoring `ios/` drops ios/README.md from format check
findings.summary: Adding `ios/` drops `ios/README.md` from the format check. On main, nothing under `SwitchboardMobile/` was excluded, and the root README and `desktop/README.md` stay covered.
findings.failure_scenario: A badly formatted edit to `ios/README.md` passes `make check` and CI, while the same edit to `desktop/README.md` fails. The ignore buys nothing else: the only other non-Swift files tracked under `ios/` are xcconfig, plist, pbxproj and shell files, none of which match prettier's globs, and build output there is already gitignored.

content.text:
I found 7 issues, listed above. Fix the first two before merging. Both come from `.gitignore` dropping the old-path rules instead of keeping them alongside the new ones:

- **Untracked personal files.** After pulling, a developer's Apple team id file (`Local.xcconfig`) and generated binaries at the old iOS path show up as untracked, so a later `git add -A` would commit them.
- **`make check` fails.** Prettier now scans leftover SwiftPM build files at the old iOS path, so `make check` fails for anyone who built the iOS package before the move.

Restoring the four old-path ignore lines fixes both. The other five are cleanup:

- Two Makefile issues: `make test`, `make lint` and `make test-browser` lack the new install step, and `make dev` now runs an install on every start.
- Two docs still use pre-move commands: `AGENTS.md` and the perf test's run instructions.
- `.prettierignore` now skips `ios/README.md`.
